title: Mystery Samples

beats.narrativeText: Inside the station laboratory, several unidentified samples remain carefully catalogued but incompletely labelled.
Atlas reminds the learner that scientists classify by evidence, not appearance alone.
The learner observes the properties of each sample carefully.
Grouping similar specimens reveals patterns among the samples.
The learner must record evidence and justify how each sample was classified.
The learner successfully classifies the samples using observable properties rather than assumptions.
The learner reflects on how classifying by evidence differs from judging by appearance alone.
The classified samples uncover another area of the expedition's research, and the laboratory records begin making sense.

activities.title: Observe Sample Properties
activities.storyContext: Several unidentified samples remain carefully catalogued but incompletely labelled in the station laboratory.
activities.instructions: Observe each sample carefully and record its properties — colour, texture, size and any other details.
activities.output: A list of observed properties for each sample.

activities.title: Group Similar Specimens
activities.storyContext: Atlas reminds the learner that scientists classify by evidence, not appearance alone.
activities.instructions: Group the samples into categories based on their observed properties.

activities.title: Record Evidence
activities.storyContext: Clear records will help future Explorers understand how each sample was classified.
activities.instructions: Write up the evidence supporting each group you created.
activities.output: Written evidence records for each group.

activities.title: Justify Classifications
activities.storyContext: A good classification can always be explained using evidence.
activities.instructions: Explain why each sample belongs in its group, using your recorded evidence.
activities.output: A justified classification for each sample.

activities.title: Design a Classification Key
activities.storyContext: A classification key would help future Explorers sort new samples quickly.
activities.instructions: Design a simple classification key that could sort new samples into your groups.

activities.title: How Biologists Classify New Species
activities.storyContext: Classifying unidentified samples is exactly the work real biologists do.
activities.instructions: Find out how biologists classify newly discovered species.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What evidence did you use to classify the samples, rather than just their appearance?

discussionPoints: Why is it important to classify by evidence rather than appearance alone?
What surprised you about grouping the samples?
parentGuide.assessment: Look for classifications justified by recorded evidence, not just first impressions.

completionCriteria: Sample properties observed, specimens grouped, and classifications justified with recorded evidence.
